newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee seen stable despite recent fall.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee seen stable despite recent fall.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee, which has fallen just over two percent against the dollar in the past five weeks, is likely to soon stabilise, the Central Bank deputy governor said on Thursday.

"The exchange rate is largely a market-determined rate, and with the outlook on the macro-economic fundamentals strong, I would really say that it will soon stabilise itself," S. Easparathasan told Reuters in an interview.
The Sri Lankan rupee was last quoted at 59.20 to the dollar on Wednesday, down 2.35 percent since late March. The foreign exchange market was closed for the May Day holiday on Thursday.
He said there was no plan by the Central Bank to intervene in the market to stabilise the rupee.
The Central Bank usually fixes daily buying and selling rates for the dollar depending on its overseas strength and rarely intervenes in the market to support the rupee.
